**Plan 0 has opened PR #1 — Wave 0 is implemented.** Its own reported gates: `tsc` clean, `eslint` exit 0 with four custom rules active, 100 tests across 19 files, Playwright collecting, and — the part that matters — **all four lint rules exit 1 on a planted violation.** Negative controls, not just green checks.

I'm running those gates independently right now rather than taking the report, per the policy I hardened earlier. Result shortly.

## One finding invalidated my own guidance

Plan 0 discovered its earlier `7n7` fix was **incomplete**: `bd init` appends to `.gitignore` **even with `--skip-agents --skip-hooks`**. The containment is **cwd, not flags**.

That matters because I'd already written the flags-only fix into the durable dispatch preamble and onto Plan 17's bead — so every future switchboard worker would have inherited a fix that doesn't work. Corrected in all three places, plus `3co`, where it has a specific consequence: the frozen contract's `VAL-API-000` setup runs `bd init` *before* its `cd`, so fixing the stale path alone would still leave it polluting whatever repo the verifier happens to be sitting in.

Two other deviations it recorded with evidence: `scripts/allowlist` had to become `.js` (ESLint loads config through Node with no TS transform, and duplicating the list is the exact drift the mechanism prevents), and ESLint 10 forbids declaring a plugin namespace twice.

## Both other workers are refusing to over-claim

`cyi` flagged the limit of the corroboration I passed it: *"the collected counts differ (6579 vs my 6574)... the load-bearing agreement is `skipped=1`, which is the claim under dispute. I'd rather flag that the totals aren't directly comparable than let two near-numbers imply more agreement than they carry."* That's the second worker to push back on my cross-worker evidence being treated as stronger than it is — and both were right.

It's also running six review agents, and told the test-review agent about its own vacuous-test failure **by name**, instructing it to re-audit the whole suite by mentally deleting the production line each test claims to cover. It pre-named the two tests it expects to be weakest. That's better instruction than I gave it.
